To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HDPsent, our proposed hierarchical model, outperforms the existing state-of-the-art models on sentiment classification tasks.

(i) HDPsent is a new topic model that incorporates sentiment learning, (ii) the model is capable of learning sentiment aspects and topics in a nonparametric Bayesian framework, and (iii) HDPsent has been evaluated and compared with other models on two different datasets.
HDPsent is able to learn latent aspects, topics and sentiment simultaneously and can be used to analyze hierarchical data.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: 1) Can we learn topics in a nonparametric way that also incorporates sentiment information? 2) Can we learn sentiment in a nonparamtric way that also incorporates topic information? and 3) Can we learn both in a unified framework?

the following: (1) how can we learn latent topics and sentiments from text data, (2) what are the implications of this for product review analysis, and (3) how can this model be applied to hierarchical data?
the problem of combining the advantages of topic modeling, aspect level sentiment learning and non-parametric Bayesian methods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach is able to learn topics, sentiments and sentiment aspects in a single generative model that is based on the Hierarchical Dirchlet Process.
the model presented here can be used to automatically generate a hierarchical structure of topics and sentiments, while also being able to learn the number of topics and sentiment aspects.
our model is the first to combine HDP and LDA based sentiment analysis within one model, which is a very promising step towards the goal of combining topic modeling and sentiment analysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HDPsent is the first model that combines the benefits of non-parametric Bayesian topic modeling with sentiment learning.
we are able to generate sentiment topics for each aspect in the reviews, which is more informative and more accurate than the existing methods.
we present a new model for sentiment analysis which can automatically generate different word distributions for different sentiments within each single topic, which has not been done before.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HDPsent is able to learn sentiment aspects and topics simultaneously, and can be used to identify and rank the importance of different aspects for a given topic.
the HDP framework can be extended to include sentiment analysis, while preserving the benefits of the original HDP model.

the HDPsent model can be used for sentiment analysis and topic modeling in a single framework, and can be extended to other hierarchical domains such as social network data, where the HDP has been used for topic modeling.
